title: Compact synthesis: routing + embeddings customer asks (Jan 2029)
content:
One-page synthesis of recurring customer signals (hosted + dedicated + private) around two tightly coupled problem areas: request routing variability (latency/cost mismatches) and embeddings reliability/drift. Drafted after: 5 customer calls (Dec 2028–Jan 2029), cross-team triage with infra + serving + cs (2029-01-08).

Topline summary
- Problem framing: customers are seeing unpredictable unit economics and occasional semantic regressions in downstream features that rely on embeddings (search, clustering). The immediate pain is operational: spikes in per-token cost due to suboptimal routing and hard-to-debug embedding quality drops after model rollouts or quantization changes.
- Impact: medium-to-high for enterprise GA customers (10–25% of requests affected in sample corpora), blocking some mid-market renewals where legal/regulatory SLAs require predictability.
- Asks (high-level): better routing transparency & controls, embedding stability guarantees + drift detection, fast rollback paths for model/quantization changes, and cheaper compatible fallback models.

Observed signals & representative customer quotes
- Signal A — routing variance (frequency: common)
  - "Our latency SLO is 200ms p95 but last week it jumped to 450ms after a capacity event; we got billed at a much higher tier and had to eat it." — fintech customer
  - Root-cause hypotheses: (1) burst routing to higher-cost region/model when local pools saturate, (2) autoscaler knob/misconfig that favors throughput-bound runtimes with higher per-token cost.
- Signal B — embedding drift & inconsistency (frequency: occasional, high severity)
  - "Search relevance regressed overnight after a model switch — the nearest neighbors changed a lot and our product team lost confidence." — marketplace customer
  - Potential drivers: model version mismatch between generate/serve, quantization-induced representational shifts, or subtle preprocessing differences at tokenization time.
- Signal C — opaque billing buckets (frequency: common)
  - Customers can't map an invocation to a cost delta (route/model/kernel) quickly enough to triage incidents.
  - Requests: per-request cost attribution, sample-level debug snapshots (kv-cache size, batch-size, chosen kernel), and a dry-run cost estimator for plan changes.

Concrete feature requests collected (ranked by frequency + impact)
1) Route-sensitivity controls (HIGH priority)
   - Allow customers to opt into: "cost-first" vs "latency-first" routing; per-route policy overrides; explicit region pinning at route-level.
   - Minimal UX: toggle + numeric budget per-route; API flag to request lower-cost variants.
2) Per-request cost & route trace (HIGH)
   - Streaming trace in Console and API with: selected model variant, kernel, region, batch size estimate, and final cost attribution. Integration point: Console traces + token-level cost breakdown.
3) Embedding-stability monitor (MED-HIGH)
   - Automated daily drift check: sample corpus embedding distribution stats, KS test vs baseline, top-10 neighbor churn metric, alerting with example queries.
   - Optional: locking policy that prevents model/quantization rollouts for specific customer projects unless embedding regression threshold passed.
4) Quantization rollback playbook + lightweight fallback model (MED)
   - Ability to fallback on a lower-precision but more stable variant or previous quantization snapshot with zero-change API mapping.
5) Dry-run cost estimator and projection API (MED)
   - Given a workload sample, return expected p50/p95 latency and per-token cost across routing policy options.
6) Tokenization/transform parity checker (LOW-MED)
   - Tool to compare preprocessing outputs across model variants/deployments to surface silent differences.

Quick sketches of proposed implementations (ops-friendly)
- Route-sensitivity controls
  - Config: route.policy = {priority: "latency" | "cost" | "balanced", max_cost_per_token: <micros>}
  - Runtime: routing decision tree checks route policy before fallbacking; log decision and reason.
- Embedding-stability monitor
  - Backend job: nightly embed sample N=2k per project, compute mean cosine, variance, neighbor-churn; raise alert if neighbor-churn > 0.12 AND mean cosine delta > 0.06.
  - Expose a threshold override in Console with a "hold-rollouts" checkbox.

Metrics / sample numbers to justify prioritization
- From 3 enterprise accounts: observed p95 latency spikes correlated with routing fallback events caused ~18% higher cost for affected requests (sample week).
- Embedding churn: a marketplace customer reported top-5 neighbor churn of 0.34 after switching to a 4-bit quantized variant; human evals showed a 12% drop in relevance.

Open questions / edge cases
- How do we attribute cost for multiplexed requests where a single user request fans out to multiple model calls (rerank + generate + embed)? Proposal: attribute to primary route and attach supplemental line items.
- For Private deployments (on-prem), we may not have the same telemetry; need a minimal local collector spec and a privacy-preserving aggregate upload or a fully offline drift checker customer can run.
- Should the "hold-rollouts" policy be customer-configurable per environment (prod/staging) or per project? Leaning per-project.

Risks and non-goals
- We should not promise zero-drift; embedding drift is expected with model changes. The goal is detection + mitigation guardrails, not guaranteed invariance.
- Heavy instrumentation can add latency. Keep traces optional and sample-based for high-volume accounts.

Immediate next steps (owner, timeframe)
- 2029-01-19: product + infra sync to align on data points needed for per-request trace (owner: Luca). Jira OPT-4123 assigned.
- 2029-01-26: prototype nightly embedding-drift job (owner: Mei) + simple Console UI mock.
- 2029-02-09: pilot with 2 willing enterprise customers; collect baseline and response data (owner: Jordan).

Notes-to-self / meeting prep
- Bring examples of the churned neighbor lists for the marketplace customer.
- Draft simple cost attribution spec and share with billing team before infra sync.
- Ask legal about telemetry sharing for Private customers (minimal aggregate only).

Useful links
- OPT-4123 (tracing & routing requirements)
- Confluence: embedding-drift-observability (detailed math + previous experiments)
- GH PR 982: earlier experimental dry-run estimator (has workload sampling utils)

Unresolved
- Exact numeric thresholds for alerts (we proposed KS + neighbor-churn combos above) — need product + CS agreement.
- Billing UX: whether to show estimated cost on per-request live traces or only aggregated daily views.

If you want a condensed slide for exec: I can extract top 3 asks + estimated effort in a 1-slide format for next PTM.
